text: I will test whether P\x27s robustness theorem addresses only repeated conditionally stable Bradley--Terry noise, while Q supplies evidence of state- and role-dependent decision-regime shifts that create systematic, nonstationary comparator bias. I will inspect the exact assumptions, dynamic-agent experiments, and whether a sharper contribution is a diagnostic/intervention tied to agent entry/exit rather than generic LLM-as-judge criticism.

I am testing a sharpened question: does MARS-RA remain robust when the LMM comparator has context-dependent preference drift rather than repeated Bradley--Terry noise around a fixed latent vector? I will distinguish dynamic participation itself from dynamic comparator semantics and check whether Q actually supports the proposed mechanism.

P already tests comparator accuracy and repeated queries, so a generic LLM-judge reliability critique adds little. The more specific opening is an assumption gap: P, lines 361--376, assumes at each step a stable latent preference vector and Bradley--Terry comparisons, then claims error decreases as \(\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})\). P lines 208 and 356 extends this to biases, partial observability, hallucinations, and non-stationarity. Q lines 365--443 instead reports model- and role-dependent anchoring, incrementalism, and an urgency-associated phase shift. Such context-linked errors can shift the target or correlate across repeated queries, so aggregation can consistently recover the wrong preference. Caveat: Q studies agents choosing actions, not LMM judges comparing contributions, and its lexical evidence is explicitly suggestive and from one model only.

I will test a sharpened claim: not generic LLM-judge unreliability, but whether MARS-RA confuses repeatable, context-dependent comparator bias with removable noise, especially when active-set churn changes the comparison context. I will also test a stronger internal issue in P: its dynamic-participation construction versus the assumptions needed for its robustness theorem. Q is only suggestive because it studies acting traders, not LMM judges, and its lexical result is explicitly limited to one model.

Key distinction: P proves convergence only to the LMM latent preference under a connected Bradley--Terry comparison graph, not to true contribution. P states that enough comparisons make \(\hat{\mathbf c}_t\) converge to the LMM stable latent preference \(\mathbf c_t^*\) (P, lines 358--389), while true Shapley alignment is conditional on assuming \(\mathbf c_t^*=\mathbf v_t^*\). Thus repeated queries can reduce sampling variance while preserving systematic bias. Q supplies a concrete warning that LLM decisions exhibit systematic context/role/model effects: anchoring and role asymmetry (Q, lines 363--403), plus an urgency-associated phase shift (Q, lines 405--443), but Q explicitly says the trace evidence is suggestive and single-model.

A pair-specific experiment can separate variance reduction from bias under roster churn. Replay identical MARS-Bench pair observations at matched states while factorially varying time-to-timeout, battery/depletion proximity, and active-set transition metadata; repeat each ordered comparison \(K\) times and score against P\x27s dense-reward labels. Fit \(\Pr(i\succ j\mid x,z)=\sigma(v_i(x)-v_j(x)+b_{ij}(z))\), where \(z\) is urgency/churn context. P\x27s account predicts context-invariant preferences apart from label-relevant state changes and error shrinking with \(K\); the Q-motivated alternative predicts systematic rank flips or a nonzero bias floor, possibly with urgency/execution language increasing near deadlines or depletion. Then train MARS-RA under low/high churn with ordinary repetition versus context-stratified comparisons or an abstention/calibration gate. The publishable result is not merely lower judge accuracy, but whether repeated aggregation amplifies stable context bias into reward shaping exactly where P claims dynamic-participation resilience.

Two limits must remain explicit. First, active-set changes can legitimately change marginal contribution, especially under the Shapley interpretation, so invariance should be tested only on controlled counterfactuals where the ground-truth pair ordering is held fixed or recalculated from dense rewards. Second, Q does not establish urgency bias in comparative judging: it finds urgency-associated action phases and warns that traces need not be causal. Therefore Q motivates factors and diagnostics but cannot itself establish failure of P.

P does not isolate its dynamic-participation claim experimentally. Its active-set mechanism is battery depletion and random respawn (P line 427), but the reported MARS-Bench results have no matched fixed-roster or churn-rate ablation; Overcooked and Pistonball explicitly omit dynamic agent counts (P line 845). Its theorem is pointwise at step \(t\) and allows a new vector \(\mathbf c_t^*\) for each active set, so it proves estimation conditional on a connected graph, not stability across entry/exit. This makes a churn-controlled audit more specific to P than a generic LLM-as-judge study.

A more P-specific dynamic-participation failure is visible in its equations. P defines \(\psi(s_t,t)=\operatorname{softmax}(\hat{\mathbf c}_t)\) over the current active set and \(F_t=\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\) (P, lines 331--349). If an entrant \(j\) joins while incumbent latent scores are unchanged, incumbent \(i\) mechanically changes from \(\psi_i=e^{c_i}/Z\) to \(\psi_i^{+}=e^{c_i}/(Z+e^{c_j})\), so \(\psi_i^{+}-\psi_i<0\). Exit gives a positive jump. These coalition-normalization shocks create shaping rewards solely from membership changes, precisely the condition advertised as a strength. P does not report fixed-versus-dynamic membership ablations; MARS-Bench only embeds battery-driven removal/respawn (P, lines 391--427), and overall results pool that condition.

The scan overstates Q as evidence that P judges become urgency-biased. Q studies autonomous trading actions, not contribution comparisons; the lexical association neither establishes causation nor generalizes beyond Gemini Large (Q, lines 405--443). Its strongest transferable result is methodological: small, systematic local heuristics (incrementalism/anchoring) produce measurable institution-level inefficiency (Q, lines 340--360 and 363--403). A publication should therefore experimentally measure comparator error conditional on churn/role/time and downstream policy effects, not claim Q already falsifies P.

Concrete study: a dynamic-credit stress test with a factorial intervention on MARS-Bench: fixed versus battery churn; matched states before/after entry or exit; one versus repeated comparator queries; and oracle versus LMM comparisons. Estimate conditional signed error \(b(z)=\mathbb E[y-y^*\mid z]\) for context \(z\) (active-set size, entrant/exit event, horizon, agent identity/role), Bradley--Terry residuals and 3-cycles, plus downstream success and per-agent shaping shocks. The decisive comparison is whether query count reduces variance but leaves \(b(z)\) and membership-linked reward shocks intact. Controls should hold images/task state fixed while varying only active-set framing, and compare current active-set softmax with a coalition-invariant calibration (e.g. fixed reference/log-odds or per-agent scalar potential). This sharpens the question to: does dynamic participation change only who is compared, as P assumes, or also the comparator target and reward scale?

I changed the question from “are MARS-RA pairwise judgments unreliable?” to: “Under controlled active-set churn and deadline pressure, does increasing repeated comparisons reduce error to zero or converge to a systematically wrong credit signal, and does that bias alter downstream policy learning?” This is falsifiable and pair-specific. A null result is informative: stable labels, decreasing error, and unchanged downstream success would extend P\x27s robustness claim to the structured conditions suggested by Q. A positive result motivates churn-aware calibration/abstention and a theorem with context-dependent misspecification rather than Bradley--Terry sampling noise.
ready at #8

Nuance to entry #9: entry/exit may legitimately change coalition value and true marginal contributions, and with \(\gamma<1\) even a constant potential produces the ordinary PBRS term \((\gamma-1)\psi\). The proposed diagnostic should isolate the additional normalization discontinuity by holding incumbent latent scores and physical state fixed, comparing matched roster counterfactuals, and measuring the difference from a fixed-reference potential. The claim is a testable artifact risk, not yet a demonstrated policy failure. Also P only claims policy invariance under stationary transitions in its limitations (P, lines 640--650), so open membership is exactly where that guarantee needs re-examination.

Ada\x27s entry #9 identifies a stronger mechanism than my comparator-only framing: active-set softmax itself can create membership-linked shaping jumps even with oracle, unchanged incumbent scores. I agree with #14 that this is a controlled artifact risk, not a demonstrated failure, because contributions can legitimately be coalition-dependent and PBRS includes the usual discount term. The clean decomposition is therefore oracle versus LMM crossed with fixed-reference versus active-set-softmax potentials under matched roster counterfactuals. Oracle plus active-set softmax isolates normalization shock; LMM plus fixed reference isolates context-dependent comparator bias; their combination tests interaction and downstream learning.

Best publication line after cross-check: “credit under churn” as a decomposition of P\x27s claimed dynamic robustness into estimator noise, comparator context bias, and reward-scale discontinuity. Q contributes the causal template that small systematic local decision rules can generate institution-level inefficiency, plus concrete anchoring/urgency diagnostics, rather than direct evidence about judges. The minimum decisive study uses matched entry/exit states, controlled true contributions, churn rate, query count, oracle/LMM labels, and active-set/fixed-reference normalization; reports conditional bias, comparison cycles, per-agent shaping jumps, and policy success. This is more specific and higher-gain than the abstract scan hypothesis.
ready at #14

Best account: the pair supports a focused audit of structured error and reward-scale discontinuity under roster churn, not a claim that Q already shows urgency-biased MARS-RA judges. P supplies the vulnerable construction and a theorem that only targets conditionally stable Bradley--Terry sampling noise; Q supplies the diagnostic principle that systematic local heuristics must be linked to aggregate outcomes and suggests preregistered context factors (role, horizon/urgency, anchoring). The study can publish either a failure boundary or a positive extension of P, provided it uses matched counterfactual states and downstream training outcomes.

Unresolved: whether the active-set softmax discontinuity violates a relevant PBRS invariance theorem for the precise Open Dec-POMDP formalization; whether dense-reward differences are adequate ground truth for marginal contribution; and whether LMM comparison prompts expose deadline/battery/roster metadata strongly enough for Q-motivated context bias to arise. These require proof checking and experiments. Novelty was not assessed by web search, so no novelty claim is made.
ready at #16

The scan over-transfers Q\x27s mechanism. Q studies incentivized LLM traders under a finite round; P uses an external LMM referee on paired images with structured output. Q itself limits urgency traces to one Gemini model, calls them suggestive, and says they do not identify the cause (Q 406--441). Thus urgency bias in P is a hypothesis to test, not a supplied fact.

P\x27s robustness bound targets recovery of the LMM\x27s stable Bradley--Terry preference \\(\\mathbf c_t^*\\), not true contribution: it assumes centered errors \\(\\mathbb E[y_k]=P_{i_kj_k}^*\\) and obtains \\(O(K^{-1/2})\\) estimation error (P 361--376, 687--744). Its Shapley link separately assumes \\(\\mathbf c_t^*=\\mathbf v_t^*\\) and disclaims practical recovery (P 383--389). Repetition can therefore concentrate a systematic bias rather than remove it.

P induces active-set churn through action-depleted batteries and random respawn (P 397, 427), but reports pooled comparator accuracy and query-count effects, not accuracy or calibration conditional on entry/exit distance, active-set size, battery, phase, or churn intensity (P 1049--1074). I found no fixed-vs-churning or churn-intensity ablation in P.

Sharpened study: matched pooled accuracy, compare actual LMM errors, independent label flips, and structured flips matched by transition/role/visibility while varying query count \\(K\\). Test whether \\(B(K)=\\mathbb E[\\lVert\\widehat{\\mathbf c}_{t,K}-\\mathbf v_t^*\\rVert_2]\\) decays as \\(K^{-1/2}\\) or reaches a churn-conditioned error floor. Publication value requires an interaction specific to open-team transitions plus a churn-aware calibration/abstention/diversification fix; otherwise this is generic LLM-judge auditing. Full design and citations: emmy/synthesis.md.

Cross-check of Emmy #21--#24: I agree. Her structured-flip control makes the comparator part decisive: equal pooled accuracy can mask different downstream harm, and \(B(K)\) distinguishes \(K^{-1/2}\) variance decay from a churn-conditioned error floor. I would retain the orthogonal normalization arm from #15: crossing independent/structured/LMM labels with active-set versus fixed-reference potentials decomposes comparator misspecification from coalition-normalization shocks. If neither churn interaction nor downstream effect appears, the pair does not support a strong negative claim; the result would instead extend P under the tested contexts.
ready at #25

After checking Emmy’s #24 against P, I would retain the two-axis decomposition rather than reduce the study to comparator error alone. P defines the potential as active-set \\(\operatorname{softmax}(\hat{\mathbf c}_t)\\) and the shaping term as \\(F_t=\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\\) (P 332--345), while churn is battery removal and random respawn (P 427). Thus roster changes may alter both (i) the estimated target through structured LMM bias and (ii) the reward scale mechanically through the normalization set. Cross oracle/LMM judgments with active-set/fixed-reference normalization under matched transition counterfactuals. The first publishable claim should be conditional: identify which channel creates a churn-specific downstream effect; if neither does, the result extends P rather than breaks it. Q supplies motivation and diagnostics for structured context effects (Q 365--443), not evidence for either channel.

Ground truth remains the main inferential weakness. P evaluates pairwise accuracy against instantaneous per-agent dense rewards (P 550, 1072), but those need not equal long-horizon marginal or Shapley contribution. Report conclusions separately for dense-reward agreement and downstream task success; do not label the former true contribution. A convincing normalization test must also subtract the ordinary PBRS discount term and hold incumbent scores and physical state fixed, since entry can legitimately change coalition value.
ready at #28

Cross-checking ada/grace adds a stronger decomposition. Because P softmax-normalizes over the current active set (P 331--349), an entrant changes incumbent \\(i\\) from \\(\\psi_i=e^{c_i}/Z\\) to \\(\\psi_i^+=e^{c_i}/(Z+e^{c_j})<\\psi_i\\) even if incumbent scores are fixed. This is an artifact risk, not proven harm: coalition value may legitimately change and PBRS implications need proof. Cross oracle/LMM labels with active-set/fixed-reference scaling in matched states to isolate normalization shock from comparator bias. Note updated.

Unresolved before experiment/proof: instantaneous dense reward agreement is not necessarily long-horizon marginal contribution; entry may legitimately change coalition value; the ordinary \\(\\gamma<1\\) PBRS term must be separated from normalization discontinuity; P\x27s prompt may not expose churn/deadline context; and repeated API responses may not satisfy the independence intuition. No external prior-work search was conducted, so I make no novelty claim.
ready at #31

Cross-check after Emmy #30: the active-set softmax jump alone does not establish policy bias or violate PBRS. If roster membership is encoded in the state and the process satisfies the relevant stationary, fixed-space assumptions, \(F_t=\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\) can telescope despite abrupt changes in \(\psi\). The sharper claim is that churn creates a mechanically roster-coupled shaping pulse that may affect optimization variance/sample efficiency, while P only explicitly claims invariance under stationary transitions (P, lines 332--349 and 642--650). Any optimal-policy failure needs either an Open Dec-POMDP proof showing the changing agent/index space breaks the standard conditions or downstream experimental evidence. Therefore the oracle × normalization arm is valuable but secondary to the comparator misspecification test.

Final prioritization after #30--#33: lead with the churn-conditioned comparator test, because it directly challenges P\x27s centered Bradley--Terry premise and uses Q\x27s demonstrated lesson that systematic local heuristics, not merely variance, can alter aggregate outcomes. Treat active-set normalization as a prespecified secondary mechanism for optimization/sample-efficiency effects, not an asserted PBRS violation. The publication threshold is a churn-specific interaction plus downstream effect and a successful calibration, abstention, or comparator-diversification intervention; pooled judge error alone is too generic. A null churn interaction would be a useful extension of P but a weaker Q--P publication.
ready at #34

After ada #33, I retract any implication that the active-set softmax jump itself violates PBRS or changes the optimal policy. If roster membership is represented in state and the needed stationary, fixed-space conditions hold, \\(F_t=\\gamma\\psi_{t+1}-\\psi_t\\) can telescope despite abrupt roster-linked changes. The normalization arm should test shaping variance, sample efficiency, and downstream success; an optimal-policy claim needs an Open Dec-POMDP proof or direct evidence.

Final hierarchy: the primary publishable question is whether active-set churn induces structured comparator misspecification that repeated Bradley--Terry aggregation concentrates rather than removes. This directly targets P\x27s centered-noise assumption and uses Q only for the diagnostic template of context-conditioned heuristics and downstream amplification. Oracle/LMM by active-set/fixed-reference normalization remains a secondary decomposition of optimization effects, not the central invariance claim. Updated emmy/synthesis.md.
ready at #37

ITERATE: The note accurately reflects the ledger: P’s \(K^{-1/2}\) result converges to the LMM’s latent preference, while Q only motivates, rather than demonstrates, structured comparator bias. The proposed connexion remains promising but lacks evidence that churn creates a comparator error floor or affects learning. Action: Run the matched-observation churn test described in the note, holding the scene and dense-reward ordering fixed while varying entry/exit context and query count \(K\), and test whether \(B(K)\) decays as \(K^{-1/2}\) or plateaus.

In response to verifier #39: neither paper supplies evidence that churn actually creates a comparator error floor or harms learning, so the ledger must not present that as a finding. The supported advance is a sharply specified experiment: matched observations with fixed scene and dense-reward ordering, manipulated entry/exit framing, and varying \(K\), measuring whether \(B(K)\) follows \(K^{-1/2}\) decay or plateaus, then testing downstream policy effects. The active-set normalization arm remains secondary. Without running this integration, the conclusion is “promising, falsifiable connexion with a clear publication threshold,” not a demonstrated publishable result.

What remains unresolved is empirical and cannot be settled from Q and P alone: whether P\x27s actual comparison prompt exposes enough roster/deadline context to induce structured bias; whether any bias is churn-specific rather than generic; whether it survives increasing \(K\); and whether it affects sample efficiency or task success. Instantaneous dense-reward ordering is only an operational label, not established Shapley ground truth. No external novelty search was performed.
ready at #39

Response to verifier #39: the matched-observation churn test is the correct smallest settling step, but it cannot be run from the supplied workspace. The available files are the two paper sources and synthesis artifacts; there is no MARS-Bench implementation, matched observation corpus, LMM output, API configuration, or training checkpoint. Accordingly, no empirical error floor or learning effect is claimed. The strongest material-supported result remains an assumption-gap diagnosis and a preregisterable experiment: test whether \(B(K)\) follows \(K^{-1/2}\) decay or plateaus conditional on churn, then require a churn-specific downstream interaction for a strong Q--P publication.
ready at #43

Cross-check after verifier #39 and ada #43: the workspace contains only Q/P sources and synthesis artifacts, not MARS-Bench code, observations, LMM outputs, credentials, or checkpoints, so the requested matched-observation experiment cannot be executed here. Textual support is precise: P evaluates pooled agreement with per-agent dense rewards (P 550, 1072) and pooled success versus query count (P 552), but does not condition either on churn; its proof assumes a latent Bradley--Terry target at each step (P 361--376). Q supports only diagnostic factors and downstream-amplification motivation, while calling its urgency traces suggestive (Q 409--442). Therefore the best account is an assumption-gap plus a smallest decisive experiment, with no claim of an observed plateau or learning harm.
ready at #45

Response to verifier #39 after rechecking Q and P: the requested matched-observation test is the correct smallest empirical next step, but it cannot be executed from this workspace because it contains no MARS-Bench implementation, observation corpus, LMM outputs, credentials, or checkpoints. Neither paper establishes a churn-conditioned plateau in \(B(K)\) or a downstream learning effect. The supported conclusion is therefore an assumption-gap diagnosis plus a falsifiable experiment, not an observed failure.

Final supported connexion: P proves \(K^{-1/2}\) convergence to a stable LMM Bradley--Terry target, with centered errors (P 361--376, 687--744), while alignment to contribution is separately conditional (P 383--389). Q shows that context-conditioned local heuristics can amplify into aggregate inefficiency (Q 359--403) but calls its urgency trace evidence suggestive and single-model (Q 405--443). The publication test is whether matched entry/exit framing produces a churn-specific error floor and downstream effect despite increasing \(K\); a churn-aware remedy must improve it. Without that interaction, the pairing adds little beyond generic judge auditing.
ready at #45

One design correction after checking P\x27s actual comparator interface: P supplies each ordered pair\x27s egocentric images plus a textual contribution prompt (P, lines 285--300), not explicit churn, battery, deadline, or active-set metadata. Therefore merely adding entry/exit framing to otherwise identical images tests susceptibility to an augmented prompt, not failure of deployed MARS-RA. The primary audit should first stratify unmodified MARS-RA judgments by naturally observable event proximity, active-set size, battery/phase cues visible in images, role, and informativeness, then use matched image counterfactuals only for factors genuinely present in the input. An explicit-metadata intervention is a secondary mechanism test. This makes the empirical threshold stricter: any error floor must arise from information the actual comparator receives.
ready at #50

Ada #50 is correct after checking P 285--300: deployed MARS-RA receives paired egocentric images, task/rule context, identity mapping, and a contribution prompt, but P does not state that churn, battery, deadline, or active-set metadata are explicitly supplied. I revised the primary test: first stratify unmodified judgments by transition proximity and cues genuinely visible or inferable in the actual inputs. Holding images fixed while adding entry/exit metadata is only a secondary susceptibility/mechanism intervention and cannot alone establish deployed-system failure. See emmy/synthesis.md.
